subtitle: Crossing of Aug 30, 2026: Polymarket price in the confirmed reading of Aug 30, 4:40 PM BRT (7:40 PM UTC), presidential book at USD 139.76M, against Vox Brasil of Aug 29 (BR-05519/2026, fieldwork Aug 25 to 27, n=2,100), which is still the most recent national poll RELEASED. This Sunday had no new national poll, and the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) registry lists eight national polls scheduled for release between Aug 31 and Sep 3, among them Datafolha and Quaest.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 55.50% (vol USD 9.50M accumulated), confirmed reading of Aug 30, 4:40 PM BRT (7:40 PM UTC). No change on the day. POLLING: Vox Brasil of Aug 29 (BR-05519/2026, fieldwork Aug 25 to 27, n=2,100) puts him at 37.1% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), 2.3 points ahead, and at 44.5% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) against 45.1%, behind by 0.6 point inside the 2.15pp margin. No national poll was released this Sunday.
fortes: He remains ahead in the first round in every national poll in the window, and Vox of Aug 29 keeps him on top with 37.1%, against 34.8% for the runner-up.

He wins both runoff scenarios that do not involve his direct opponent in the same Vox poll: 45.5% to 39.3% against Romeu Zema and 45.5% to 41.1% against Ronaldo Caiado, both outside the 2.15pp margin.

His campaign opened an offensive at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) against his opponent, Caiado and Zema over posts and speeches this Sunday, according to Folha de S.Paulo, and asked for his opponent to be declared ineligible for economic abuse, according to Metrópoles.
His outright-winner contract is still at 55.50%, more than 14 points above the runner-up, and the presidential book holds USD 139.76M.
In Quaest's state-by-state series released this week he leads in seven states, the same number as his opponent, according to SpaceMoney.
fracos: Vox of Aug 29 puts him BEHIND in a runoff scenario: 44.5% against 45.1%. The 0.6 point difference sits inside the 2.15pp margin and is a [technical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico). Across the two Vox readings the sign of the runoff changed sides: on Jul 31 the leader was 6.4 points ahead and now he is 0.6 point behind. That holds for the Vox series, not for the set of national polls. In the panel's 30-day window he had already appeared ahead in the runoff in three other national polls: Gerp of Aug 26, 47% to 42%, Veritá of Aug 21, 47.3% to 42%, and Gerp of Aug 11, 45% to 43%. The pollsters disagree with each other about the runoff, and the clearest case is Aug 26, when Gerp gave him 47% to 42% and Indexa/Broadcast gave the leader 46% to 41%, on the SAME day and with opposite signs.

Comparing Vox with itself exactly one month later, he gives ground on everything: 40.5% to 37.1% in the first round and 47.5% to 44.5% in the runoff. The first-round distance fell from 9.3pp to 2.3pp, a drop of 7 points, which Exame also reported.
His rejection stands at 52.7% in the same Vox poll, above the opponent's 49.3%, according to CNN Brasil. Disapproval of him is 53.3% in the same round, according to Exame.

The outright-winner price has not moved since Friday afternoon, across nine consecutive captures in the series, and the distance to the runner-up fell to 14.40pp, the narrowest since Jun 10. All of the narrowing over the past 24 hours came from his opponent's side.
The case involving his son remains under Federal Police investigation and keeps the campaign under pressure, according to the BBC.
candidates.analise: Sunday pulled the two measurements apart, and that separation is the record of the day. The declared ballot had no new reading: Vox Brasil of Aug 29 (BR-05519/2026, fieldwork Aug 25 to 27, n=2,100) is still the most recent national poll released, with the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) at 37.1% to 34.8% and the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) at 45.1% to 44.5% for the runner-up, inside the margin. The price did move, and it moved on one side only. He has been stuck at 55.50% (vol USD 9.50M) since Friday afternoon, across nine consecutive captures, while his opponent rose 1.75pp. The distance between the two closed at 14.40pp, the narrowest since June 10. The TSE registry lists eight national polls scheduled for release between Aug 31 and Sep 3, three of them on Monday, among them the first Datafolha presidential poll after the candidates' TV Globo interviews. Registration is not release, and none of their numbers enters the panel before it is out. Until then the panel serves a fresh price and a Friday poll, and it says so.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 41.10% (vol USD 9.31M accumulated), confirmed reading of Aug 30, 4:40 PM BRT (7:40 PM UTC). Up 1.75pp, the largest move among the panel's names this round, and his highest price since May 13. POLLING: Vox Brasil of Aug 29 (BR-05519/2026, fieldwork Aug 25 to 27, n=2,100) puts him at 34.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and at 45.1% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), ahead of the leader by 0.6 point and inside the margin.
fortes: Vox Brasil of Aug 29 puts him numerically AHEAD in the runoff, 45.1% to 44.5%. The 0.6 point difference sits inside the 2.15pp margin, so it is a [technical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico). Across the two Vox readings the sign of the runoff changed sides: on Jul 31 the leader was 6.4 points ahead and now he is 0.6 point behind. In the panel's 30-day window he had already appeared ahead in the runoff in three other national polls: Gerp of Aug 26, 47% to 42%, Veritá of Aug 21, 47.3% to 42%, and Gerp of Aug 11, 45% to 43%. The pollsters disagree with each other about the runoff, and the clearest case is Aug 26, when Gerp gave him 47% to 42% and Indexa/Broadcast gave the leader 46% to 41%, on the SAME day and with opposite signs.

Comparing Vox with itself one month later, he rises on everything: 31.2% to 34.8% in the first round and 41.1% to 45.1% in the runoff. That is 3.6pp and 4.0pp, with the same in-person method and the same sample.

The outright-winner contract rose 1.75pp this Sunday, to 41.10%, the largest move among the panel's names this round, and it is his highest price since May 13. In the first-round second-place contract he sits at 85.50%.
His rejection, at 49.3%, is LOWER than the leader's 52.7% in the same Vox poll, according to CNN Brasil.
He debuted on radio betting on the economy, family and security, according to Estadão and InfoMoney, and leads in seven states in Quaest's series, tied with the leader on that count.
fracos: He remains behind in the first round in every national poll in the window, including Vox of Aug 29, which puts him at 34.8% against 37.1%.

He refused to account for the Dark Horse case and tried to tie Banco Master to his opponent, according to Folha de S.Paulo, on a day when his audio with the former banker returned to campaign advertising.
The leader called him an amateur and an adventurer over his TV Globo interview, according to Gazeta do Povo, and the interview became a point of comparison between the two.
The 1.75pp rise came on a Sunday with NO national poll released, and the most recent reading has fieldwork from Aug 25 to 27. Nothing in the two measurements isolates the cause of the move.

The first-round second-place contract puts him at 85.50%, meaning the market treats his trip to the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) as close to settled and trades the rest. A high price there is not the same as a high price in the outright-winner contract, where he pays 41.10%.
candidates.analise: He is the only name on the panel that moved continuously over the past 24 hours. The price went from 39.35% on Friday to 41.10% (vol USD 9.31M) this Sunday, rising almost monotonically through the day, and it is his highest value since May 13. It is not a series high: the top is still 45.50%, from May 6. In the first-round second-place contract he sits at 85.50%, meaning the market treats his trip to the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) as close to settled and trades the rest. The declared ballot brought no new reading this Sunday, so the comparison is still with Vox of Aug 29, which puts him at 34.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and ahead by 0.6 point in the runoff, inside the margin. What the day adds is campaign fact, not measurement: he met Bukele's justice minister and said he takes inspiration from the El Salvador model, and the leader's campaign went to the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) against him on three fronts.

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: PRICE: 2.25% (vol USD 11.88M accumulated), confirmed reading of Aug 30, 4:40 PM BRT (7:40 PM UTC). No change. In the first-round third-place contract he sits at 25.00%. POLLING: Vox of Aug 29 measures him at 3.3% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), the fourth name on the table.
fortes: His book has accumulated USD 11.88M, the LARGEST among the panel's candidates, above the leader at USD 9.50M and the runner-up at USD 9.31M. Volume is not price, but it measures how much money has passed through the contract.
Vox of Aug 29 measures him at 3.3% in the first round, above Romeu Zema at 2.8% and Augusto Cury at 2.6%.
In the first-round third-place contract he sits at 25.00%, practically level with Augusto Cury at 25.45% and behind Ronaldo Caiado at 43.50%.
fracos: In the outright-winner contract he pays 2.25%, and he is the fourth name in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in Vox of Aug 29, at 3.3%. The two quantities do not subtract: one measures voting intention and the other, the chance of winning.
The outright-winner contract gave up 0.65pp, to 2.25%, giving back the two consecutive rises it had made after the Aug 27 floor.
The 2.25% remains far below the April level, when he reached 49.60%.

Dias Toffoli signed a ruling on Saturday, August 29, pulling Renan Santos and running mate Aroldo Medina’s candidacy registration off the docket of the virtual plenary session set for August 31. He pointed to signs of illegality because the ticket filed 18 social media profiles on August 19, with the registration request submitted on August 7, outside the legal deadline. The decision became public on August 30, with seven outlets publishing between 3:47 PM and 6:56 PM Brasília time. His price did not react on either Saturday or Sunday.
candidates.analise: His crossing is the most direct of the day, and the result is that there was no crossing. Dias Toffoli signed a ruling on Saturday, August 29, pulling Renan Santos and running mate Aroldo Medina’s candidacy registration off the docket of the virtual plenary session set for August 31. He pointed to signs of illegality because the ticket filed 18 social media profiles on August 19, with the registration request submitted on August 7, outside the legal deadline. The decision became public on August 30, with seven outlets publishing between 3:47 PM and 6:56 PM Brasília time. His price did not move: 2.25% (vol USD 11.88M) in the confirmed reading, the same value as Friday, and the series keeps him at 2.30% in every cron capture on Saturday and Sunday, including those after publication. His book is the third largest in the outright-winner contract, at USD 11.88M, above the leader's and the runner-up's, which makes the absence of movement harder to put down to a thin market. The panel records the fact, the date of the act and the absence of a reaction, and assigns no cause to any of the three.

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), presidential Poly 0.05% (vol USD 7.41M accumulated, confirmed reading of Aug 30, 4:40 PM BRT (7:40 PM UTC)), no change. Below the 0.5% floor of the double reading.
haddad.fortes: He is not a presidential candidate: he is running for governor of São Paulo. His presidential price is book residue, not a measure of campaign, and Vox Brasil of Aug 29 does not test him in the presidential scenario.
haddad.fracos: The 0.05% sits below the 0.5% floor of the double reading, the range where AFOS does not certify movement. The book holds USD 7.41M, almost all of it traded when the name was still tested as a presidential alternative.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), presidential Poly 0.05% (vol USD 6.37M accumulated, confirmed reading of Aug 30, 4:40 PM BRT (7:40 PM UTC)), no change. Below the 0.5% floor of the double reading.

zema.fracos: The outright-winner contract is still at 0.05%, below the watch floor, and in the first-round third-place contract he sits at 2.15%. candidates.analise: The back of the field is still where the two measurements disagree most, and Caiado's case is the sharpest on the panel. He is the THIRD name in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in Vox of Aug 29, at 5.0%, and in the outright-winner contract he sits at 0.15% (vol USD 6.97M), below the watch floor of the double reading. At the same time, he is the LEADING name in the first-round third-place contract, at 43.50%. In other words, the market pays a lot for him to finish third and almost nothing for him to win, and the two things are consistent with each other. Haddad and Zema remain at 0.05% each, and Haddad is not a presidential candidate: he is running for governor of São Paulo. Caiado joined this Sunday the offensive the leader's campaign opened at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) over posts and speeches.
fortes: RONALDO CAIADO (PSD) is the third name in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) in Vox of Aug 29, at 5.0%, and he is the LEADING name in the first-round third-place contract, at 43.50%, while in the outright-winner contract he pays 0.15%.

In the runoff scenario of the same Vox poll, Caiado loses 45.5% to 41.1%, a distance of 4.4 points, smaller than Zema's, who loses 45.5% to 39.3%.
AUGUSTO CURY (Avante) gave an interview to TV Globo this Sunday, according to BBC, and in the first-round third-place contract he sits at 25.45%.
fracos: Caiado, Zema and Haddad all remain below the 0.5% floor in the outright-winner contract, the range where the double reading does not certify movement.
Cury gave up 1.40pp in the outright-winner contract, to 1.85%, the largest drop among the panel's names this round, and his 2.6% in Vox of Aug 29 sits below the 4% PoderData/Aya gave him on Aug 27.

The entire third-place book holds USD 0.73M, less than 0.6% of the presidential book. The contest among the three names takes place in the panel's smallest market.
